Daily air temperature on FWA segments

Source: R/wet_air_daily.R
wet_air_daily.Rd

Reads daily air temperature for Freshwater Atlas stream segments from wet's published air_temperature/fwa/v1 tree: each segment's ERA5-Land cell from segment_cell, then that cell's days from cell_daily. The values are cd's daily cube (cd::cd_extract_daily()) copied unchanged, so a segment reads what cd_extract_daily() gives at the segment's midpoint, without cd, raster tooling or a download of the cube. The result has the columns wet_temp_fill() reads as air.

Usage

wet_air_daily(segments, from, to, variables = "tmean", groups, catalog = NULL)

Arguments

segments

FWA linear_feature_ids, whole numbers, none NA.

from, to

First and last day, as Date or "YYYY-MM-DD".

variables

Any of "tmean", "tmax", "tmin" (°C).

groups

Watershed group codes holding the segments (required): only their lookup parts are read. A segment outside them reads as missing.

catalog

A wet_catalog() of the air tree. The default reads option wet.air_catalog_url, or else the published air manifest.

Value

data.frame(id, date, variable, value, cell_id, cell_x, cell_y, cell_moved, cell_status), one row per segment, variable and day, ordered by segment as given, variable as given and date. id is the linear_feature_id; cell_id numbers the cell on the regular 0.1° grid ERA5-Land is distributed on (not cd's cell number); cell_moved is TRUE for a "moved" segment. A segment with no cell, or one the lookup does not hold (cell_status NA), has its days with value NA.

The cell

A segment takes the cell holding its midpoint along the line. Where that cell has no data (the coast, large lakes) it takes the nearest of the eight around it that has, as cd does (cell_status "moved"); where none of the nine has, or the midpoint is outside cd's box, it has no cell ("no_data", "outside") and its values are NA. Which cells have data is read from one day of the cube, which the manifest names. There is no elevation adjustment between the cell and the segment.

The day

A day is BC's local standard day (UTC-8), as cd defines it, so date is a calendar day, not an instant.

See also

wet_temp_fill(), which takes this as air.

Examples

# a tiny made-up tree laid out as the published one, from cd's example cube
cat <- wet_catalog(system.file("air", "manifest.json", package = "wet"))
a <- wet_air_daily(c(1, 2, 4), "2002-07-01", "2002-07-03", groups = "AAAA", catalog = cat)
